### sockets and server sockets (Python)  (1)


![](/sockets/texfig/connection-setup-sockets-and-server-sockets-python.figure-1.svg){fig-alt="on the client, a socket is created with sock = socket.socket(...); on the server a 'server socket' is created with socoket.socket(...) followed by ssock.bind(...) and listen(...)"}

### sockets and server sockets (Python)  (2)


![](/sockets/texfig/connection-setup-sockets-and-server-sockets-python.figure-2.svg){fig-alt="the socket.socket(...) function is used on both client and server to create the initial normal or server socket."}

::: {.myoverbox}

*  `socket()` function --- creates socket file descriptor
   *  arguments indicate address type, protocol
   *  initially not configured for server or client

:::
"}

### sockets and server sockets (Python)  (3)


![](/sockets/texfig/connection-setup-sockets-and-server-sockets-python.figure-3.svg){fig-alt="on the server ssock.bind(...) and ssock.listen() are run after creating the socket."}

::: {.myoverbox .lowright}

*  `listen()` --- turn socket into server socket
*  still has file descriptor, but...
   *  does not support recv/send (or read/write)
   *  can only `accept()` to create new normal socket

:::


### sockets and server sockets (Python)  (4)


![](/sockets/texfig/connection-setup-sockets-and-server-sockets-python.figure-4.svg){fig-alt="the client runs socket.connect() to request a connection, which contacts the server socket setup with listen(). The server runs ssock.accept(), which returns a new socket sock and an address addr."}


### sockets and server sockets (Python)  (5)


![](/sockets/texfig/connection-setup-sockets-and-server-sockets-python.figure-4.svg){fig-alt="the client's socket sock, on which connect() was called, now has a connection to the socket sock on the server that was just returned from accept()."}
